This is the card's recommended option, and it reuses an existing output instead of a hand-kept second recognizer of the backend's dependency graph, the choice the filter contract's half 1 argues for.

The card names the queue skip as half of the gap, so this is intended, not incidental. The merge_group trigger is present on the workflow, so the required context still reports on every queue build.

11. The head's own check-runs: `Live E2E UI` ran and concluded `success` on this PR. Note that this head would have run it under the OLD gate as well (`ci.yml` is in both the `ui` and `core` lists), so that run is evidence the job still works, not evidence of the widening; the card's two-minute verification (a `packages/objectql`-only PR runs it) is future-dated by design and follows from the expression semantics, which are identical to `build-core`'s `core` conjunct.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body; the PR carries the `skip-changeset` label and `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on the opening run (its later `skipped` runs are the `labeled` / `edited` event-action skips the roster admits). The diff publishes nothing: one workflow file, no `packages/**`, no schema, no changeset needed. The declaration matches what the diff publishes. The `Clause-②:` line is correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag: actionlint NOT MEASURED (binary download refused by the dev container's classifier; the repo and its CI carry no actionlint). Answered: the workflow parsed and ran on the head (`filter` and every gated job published a check-run), and `check:workflow-status-functions` plus `check-workflow-context-availability` are green over it. actionlint is not a gate this repo derives; nothing is owed. Not escalated.
- Dev flag: PR check-runs NOT MEASURED at report time. Answered here from the head's check-runs: 65 runs, every gated job `success`, every `skipped` run a roster shape (full-battery jobs on a per-PR event, opt-in harnesses, PR-automation event-action skips, the schedule gate). `Live E2E UI` `success`.

Not a review matter beyond that.

- `open_questions[0]`: should the `filter` job's outputs comment ("read together by the five `* UI` jobs") mention that Live E2E UI now reads `core`? The lane answered A (leave it). Judged here: the sentence about the THREE ui outputs stays true, and no gate reads that prose. But the sibling `crosspkg` comment names its one reader ("Gates the `test` job ONLY"), while the `core` output's comment names none, so a reader of the `filter` job cannot learn from it that a ui job now hangs off `core`. Classified SHOULD-FIX (a one-line note on the `core` output), not must-fix: the live job's own comment states the read, and the claim's file surface excludes other jobs, so A is a defensible reading of the claim. Not escalated.
- Card task 3 (re-run the derived gates) is answered by the head's check-runs, not by the dev's local exits: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` both `success`.

### ④ Design judgment

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, judged against card #27550's acceptance, the `filter` job's outputs and paths lists, the `build-core` / `build-e2e-ui` conditions, the live job's own steps and scripts, and the three derived gates.

Attempts to break the gate:

- A diff the new gate would SKIP that should run the job. Walked the job's inputs: `ui/e2e/live/ci/start-backend.sh`, `backend.env`, `ui/scripts/ensure-chromium-ready.sh`, `ui/playwright.live.config.ts`, `ui/e2e/live/**` (all `ui/**`); `examples/app-showcase` (`examples/**`, `core`); `packages/cli` and the whole server closure the showcase loads at runtime (`packages/**`, `core`); the lockfile, workspace file, `turbo.json`, the `tsconfig*` (in `ui` and/or `core`); `ci.yml` itself (both). Nothing the job reads at build or run time falls outside `ui || ui_consumers || core` except two pre-existing repo-wide blind spots that this diff neither opens nor claims to close: `.github/actions/**` (the composite actions every job uses) and `.nvmrc` match no filter list at all, so a diff confined to one of them starts no gated job in this workflow. Noted for the lane, not a finding against this change.
- A required check that would stop reporting. The `name:` literal is unchanged; `needs: filter` unchanged; no matrix; no `continue-on-error`; the `merge_group` and unfiltered `pull_request` triggers are unchanged. The expression stays a conjunction whose first term is `!cancelled()`, so a dead `filter` job runs the job rather than skipping it (filter contract half 2). Nothing here can produce an absence.
- A spelling the roster or the status-function gate would refuse. The new conjunct is a parenthesised `||` of three `needs.filter.outputs.X != 'false'` terms, the exact shape `gateTerm` recognises (its self-test case "a parenthesised || of filter outputs is ONE group" is this shape with two terms; the code imposes no arity). `check-workflow-status-functions` requires a status function beside any `needs.*.outputs.*` read; `!cancelled()` is present. Both gates green on the head.
- The queue-side consequence. `core` is `'true'` on every `merge_group` build, so every queue entry pays the job (roughly 1.5 to 9 minutes on the card's population). The card explicitly names the queue skip as part of the defect and the comment states the consequence; the job's `timeout-minutes: 40` bounds it. Accepted as designed.
- The wall-clock premise. The card's "no added PR wall-clock" claim rests on measurements of runs where the job already ran (ui-touching diffs). On a server-only diff the live job rebuilds the changed server packages and their dependents itself (it restores Build Core's turbo seed by prefix and builds `@objectstack/cli...` and `@objectstack/example-showcase...`), which is the same work Build Core and the Test Core shards do in parallel, so the ordering claim is plausible but not verifiable from this head. The ci.yml comment is careful here: it claims run counts, the measured alternative and the spec-step durations, not a zero-wall-clock guarantee. No defect in the tree.
- The BUDGET statement. The comment pins "Run the live e2e specs" under 2 minutes, cites 14 to 24 s over 35 runs, and routes any spec that would breach it to `test:e2e:live:nightly`. `ui/package.json` carries exactly those two scripts: `test:e2e:live:ci` with four specs (`screen-flow`, `action-modal`, `master-detail`, `saved-view-filter`) and `test:e2e:live:nightly` with fifteen. The job runs `test:e2e:live:ci --retries 0`. The comment matches the tree. The card made a duration-reading gate optional; none is added, which is within the card.
- Comment accuracy. "Gated as Build & E2E UI is, OR'd with `core`" matches the two `if:` lines. "Build & E2E UI builds the Console against the seven packages it compiles from" matches that job's seven `--filter`s. "On merge_group `core` is always 'true'" matches the `core` output expression. One imprecision, SHOULD-FIX: the parenthetical "`core` (packages/**, examples/**, apps/!(docs)/** and the root build inputs)" omits `skills/**`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and Build Core's guard scripts, all of which are in the `core` list; `skills/**` is the very set that produced the five skills-only runs the next sentence attributes to the widening, so a reader who takes the parenthetical as the list will not see why. One word ("and the root build inputs, `skills/**` among them") closes it. Not a must-fix: the sentence is a summary, the authoritative list is twenty lines above in the same file, and the five-run explanation is present.
- Card constraints: no retry wrapper and no `continue-on-error` added (the job's ⛔ line is intact; the only `continue-on-error` in the file's ui section is the pre-existing `download-artifact` fallback in `build-e2e-ui` and the cache saves, none in this job); no other job touched (the diff's two hunks are the live job's comment and its `if:`).

Findings: no must-fix. Should-fix: (1) a one-line note on the `filter` job's `core` output that Live E2E UI reads it (the dev's open question, answered A by the lane); (2) the comment's `core` parenthetical should name `skills/**` and the other non-root entries, or say "among them". Neither changes behaviour; both can land in the lane's next `ci.yml` PR.
